version.author: TwelveTake Studios
version.changelog: After you update, run twelvetake-reaper-mcp --install-bridge. If REAPER is running the 1.7.8 bridge or later, you don't have to do anything in REAPER. If you installed with ReaPack, synchronize your packages instead. Fixed: - Volume automation from add_envelope_point could play as silence. The tool described envelope values as 0.0 to 1.0, but a volume envelope's scale depends on its scaling mode. With fader scaling, REAPER stores 0 dB as 716.2, so every value from 0.0 to 1.0 was silence. A negative value, which AI clients sent when they worked in dB, was silence in either mode. You can now give a level in dB with value_db on Volume, Volume (Pre-FX) and Trim Volume, and the tool converts it for the envelope's scaling mode. If you send a negative raw value to a volume envelope, the tool refuses it and points you to value_db. *(Reported by @gitickle in issue #20.)* - The envelope tool descriptions now give the units REAPER uses. A pan envelope runs from +1 for left to -1 for right, the reverse of set_track_pan. An FX parameter envelope takes the parameter's own value, inside the range track_fx_get_param reports, so a JSFX dB slider takes dB. - get_track_items and get_selected_items left out each item's name. They now include the take name, as get_item_info does. Added: - create_click_track gives you a click track for the song, on a new track at the end of the track list. It uses REAPER's click source, so it follows tempo and time signature changes and accents each downbeat. It covers the whole project unless you give it a start and end. - Envelope points now come back as REAPER displays them. add_envelope_point, get_envelope_points, add_fx_envelope_point and get_fx_envelope_points include shown, for example "-6.00dB", "50%L" or "UNMUTE". On a volume envelope you also get value_db, and scaling, which is "fader" or "amplitude". - add_envelope_point now returns the new point's point_index, as its description said it would.
